title: Accumulator-independence of the encoder's first output
statement: Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables, a width parameter $w \in \bbn$, a fuel bound $\in \bbn$, a partial path recorded as a list of variable–value pairs $(i,b) \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n \times \{0,1\}$, and two restrictions $\rho_0, \sigma$ on the $n$ variables. The auxiliary recursion underlying the Razborov encoding takes, in addition, a starting accumulator: a list of index–bit pairs in $\bbn \times \{0,1\}$, and returns a pair. Then the first component of its output does not depend on that accumulator: running the recursion from an arbitrary accumulator yields the same first component as running it from the empty accumulator.
hypotheses_covered: DNF formula f on n variables
width parameter w in the naturals
arbitrary starting accumulator (list of index-bit pairs)
caveat: The auxiliary function razborovEncode.go is not among the supplied definitions, so what it computes and what its first output component means cannot be described from the given material; only the structural claim — that this first component is invariant under changing the starting accumulator — can be stated faithfully.
replaced:
The first component of the encoder loop \texttt{SwitchingLemma2.razborovEncode}'s
\texttt{go} does not depend on the accumulator: running with accumulator $\mathrm{acc}$
yields the same first component as running with the empty accumulator.
